lines.narration: The sun doesn't turn orange. Your sky just runs out of blue.
Sunlight looks white — but it's carrying every color at once.
Air is a sieve: molecules fling blue sideways about six times harder than red.
At noon, your beam crosses one patch of air. At sunset? Thirty-eight.
Thirty-eight times the air, and every step bleeds more blue away. What survives the whole trip is orange.
The blue that got thrown out? It never dies — it becomes the rest of your sky.
Same sun. Same air. Only the angle changed.
On Mars, dust flips the trick — blue sunsets. Go watch yours tonight.
